question: The capital of the Mauryan empire was ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pataliputra**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pataliputra** was the **capital city of the Mauryan Empire**, one of the largest and most powerful empires in ancient India.
 
• The city was strategically located near the confluence of the Ganges, Gandak, and Son rivers, making it a significant hub for trade and commerce.
 
• Under the reign of Emperor **Ashoka**, Pataliputra became a major center for learning and culture, attracting scholars from different parts of the world.
 
• The city was well-fortified with massive walls and a moat, and it had numerous palaces, gardens, and public buildings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Mauryan Empire was founded by** Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE**, and it reached its zenith under the rule of Ashoka.
 
• Ashoka, after the** Kalinga War**, embraced **Buddhism **and made significant contributions to the spread of Buddhism across Asia.
 
• The Mauryan administration was highly organized, with a complex bureaucracy and a network of spies to maintain law and order.
 
• The **Arthashastra**, an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy, is attributed to **Chanakya (Kautilya)**, who was a key advisor to Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• The decline of the Mauryan Empire began after the death of Ashoka, leading to the rise of regional kingdoms in India.
